Subject: Performance SLO qualification - follow-up & next steps

Hi Sam —

Thanks for taking the time today — great conversation and really appreciate the clarity on ACME's streaming transcription use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on SLOs and cost levers: 

Recap of SLOs you shared:
- Target p95 latency for streaming tokens: <= 200 ms end-to-end (client-side ingestion -> first token).
- Sustained throughput target: 1,200 concurrent streams during peak business hours.
- Concurrency per instance: typical single-model concurrency target is ~40-60 streams; you expect bursts to 150 concurrent streams.
- Token rate per stream: ~12 tokens/sec average (peaks to 30 tokens/sec).
- Availability/SLA ask: 99.9% for production.

Initial qualification notes (what I heard):
- Priority is latency for the first token and low tail latency for streaming.
- Cost sensitivity: want to balance latency vs unit cost; open to model/quantization tradeoffs if output quality stays acceptable.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 required (we covered our SOC 2 report), and traffic will originate from US regions.

Suggested technical levers to evaluate (we can run a short PoC):
1) Continuous batching + adaptive batching: reduces per-token cost by batching small in-flight requests without adding much tail latency for streaming. Good for stable throughput.
2) KV/prefix caching: for repeated prompts or common prefixes (meeting intros, greetings) — reduces compute and improves tail latency.
3) Quantization profiles: test 4-bit/8-bit quantized variants of the same model; often near-original quality with 2-3x compute savings.
4) Model variants: try a smaller, low-latency variant for first-token and fall back to a higher-quality variant for long-form responses (hybrid routing).
5) Smart routing & capacity tiers: reserve Dedicated capacity for guaranteed concurrency; use Hosted fallback for burst handling.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll share a brief perf questionnaire (attached) that will help us size Dedicated capacity and propose quantization profiles. Please fill and return by Tue 3/17.
- Schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough with Vivek (runtime/ops) next week to validate streaming instrumentation and sampling. Options: Mon/Wed next week 10–12 PT.
- If the perf questionnaire aligns, we’ll propose a short PoC (2 weeks) to validate p95 tail latency and cost per million tokens with 1,200 concurrent streams.

Attachments: acme_perf_requirements.pdf (short questionnaire), redwood_proposal_v1.pdf (initial commercial outline).

Thanks — I’ll follow up once I get your availability.

Best,

Sam — thanks, great questions. I asked Vivek to join here to cover runtime sizing and quality guidance. Answers at a high level below; we’ll go deeper on the tech call and in the PoC.

1) Continuous batching & first-token latency:
- Our runtime uses adaptive batch windows: short windows for low-load to avoid additional queuing (e.g., <10 ms extra), and slightly larger windows at scale to improve throughput.
- We also implement low-latency bypass: requests that hit the first-token SLO are prioritized into small micro-batches or single-request fast-paths. For streaming, first-token policy is aggressive.
- In previous PoCs, we achieved p95 first-token latencies of 120–180 ms on 7B-class models with streaming enabled and batching tuned.

2) Quantization & quality:
- We recommend testing 8-bit first; many customers see negligible WER impact. For risk-averse workloads you can run A/B quality evals (we can attach eval harness).
- If 8-bit has measurable regression, a mixed profile (8-bit for most tokens, 16-bit for critical tokens) is an option.

3) Dedicated sizing estimate (very rough):
- For a 7B model, with our optimized kernels and continuous batching, expect ~50–70 concurrent streams per GPU at 12 tokens/sec with streaming enabled.
- For 1,200 concurrent streams, that maps to ~18–24 GPUs reserved (we’ll refine after we get your token-length distribution and exact model).

PoC proposal:
- Week 0: ingest perf questionnaire + test data (you supply 1 hour sample of typical streams).
- Week 1: initial tuning on Hosted/Dedicated equivalent; measure p50/p95 first-token and steady-state throughput.
- Week 2: scale test to target concurrency and validate cost per million tokens and fallback behavior.

Action items:
- Sam: confirm Wed 3/18 10:30 PT for the tech walkthrough.
- Sam: return questionnaire by 3/17 if possible.
- Vivek & I will prepare suggested batch/quant profiles to test during PoC.

Attaching: acme_perf_requirements.pdf (filled copy will help us size).

Adding a few pragmatic notes from the runtime/ops side: 

- Telemetry & sampling: We’ll enable request-level tracing for the PoC (token timestamps, batch sizes, queue time) and supply dashboards so you can validate p95 at the client boundary.
- Warm pools & cold starts: We recommend a small warm pool to absorb bursts while autoscaling spins up additional capacity; warm pools reduce cold-start tail latencies substantially.
- Fallbacks: Configure smart routing rules: prefer Dedicated for latency-critical streams, allow Hosted fallback for unexpected >20% bursts. That keeps SLA while controlling cost.
- Cost levers to iterate during PoC:
  * Increase batching window slightly (trade small increase in median latency for 20–40% token cost reduction).
  * Test 8-bit quantization profile across a sample set — measure WER and p95 impact.
  * Try hybrid model routing: small low-latency variant for first-token, route to higher capacity variant for longer utterances.

I’ll prepare an ops checklist for Wed’s call (deployment config, telemetry links, expected test harness). Looking forward to the call.
